title: Settings: account-protection fixes, security emails, and a hash-addressed settings document
summary: Ends editor tokens on password change and deletion, requires the authenticator for destructive actions when one exists, fixes the step-up dialog and no-method dead ends, makes notification preference saves merge-only under a row lock, keeps error states honest (no defaults saved over real settings), adds a deletion preflight and manual-token step-up, and turns the Settings nav into hash anchors with observers. Adds eight account-security email kinds on the email outbox (migration 0253), a daily deletion-reminder job, disconnecting sign-in methods with fresh verification, authoritative password state from the stored credential, and more audit events. Later in the same work: a ninth email kind for the deletion-completed message (migration 0255, since 0253 was already applied), a sign-in-method-linked audit event, an account-export record and last-export lookup, legal acceptance history with a separate age assertion, per-user step-up and commit-identity limits, a clock-skew clamp on appearance timestamps, and an app-level pending-deletion strip.
concurrencyRisk: Notification preference saves lock the profile row and write only the changed top-level keys, so two tabs or a tray mute can no longer overwrite each other. Editor token revocation is a single UPDATE and idempotent.

rollback.strategy: Revert the commits. Migration 0253 only widens a CHECK constraint on email_outbox.kind: if it was applied, leaving it in place is harmless. Revoked editor tokens stay revoked (sign the editor in again); saved preferences keep their shape.
